headline: Money dispute: Man arrested for killing co-worker in Ashulia
summary: The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) solved the murder within 24 hours using biometric fingerprint technology to identify the victim.
details: The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has arrested Al-Amin for the killing of his co-worker and childhood friend, Kamrul Khan, 44, in Ashulia.

caption:
A childhood friendship ended in tragedy when a man killed his co-worker over a money dispute in Ashulia.

The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has arrested Al-Amin for the killing of his co-worker and childhood friend, Kamrul Khan, 44, in Ashulia.

A decomposed body was discovered in a locked room in Ashulia’s Basaid area on August 16 after the house owner alerted police.

PBI investigators used biometric fingerprint technology to identify the victim and arrested Al-Amin from Terokhada in Khulna on August 17.

The two men had moved from Khulna to Ashulia on August 8 to work as masons. According to investigators, the murder occurred on August 14 following an altercation over money.

Investigators say Kamrul tried to attack Al-Amin with a knife during the fight; Al-Amin snatched the knife and killed him on the spot.

Al-Amin then hid the knife in the toilet, locked the room and fled back to Khulna before giving a confessional statement before a magistrate.

The PBI is continuing the investigation to determine if anyone else was involved in the crime.

headline: Cumilla UP chairman admits beating woman with shoes during arbitration
summary: The Madhabpur Union Parishad Chairman admitted to the act after a video of the incident went viral on social media.
details: A woman was allegedly beaten with shoes by Madhabpur Union Parishad Chairman Md Farid Uddin during a village arbitration in Cumilla’s Brahmanpara upazila.
The incident occurred on August 17 and a video of the beating went viral on social media, triggering widespread anger among locals.
The arbitration was held over allegations that the woman was involved in an extramarital relationship with a man from a village under the union.
UP Chairman Farid Uddin admitted to the beating, stating that the woman had been ‘found guilty’ and he was merely carrying out the decision of the arbitrators as an elected representative.
Advocate Shahidul Haque Swapan of the Cumilla Bar Association stated that an elected representative has no legal authority to publicly beat a woman, regardless of the offence.

Brahmanpara Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Faruk Hossain said that while no formal complaint has been filed yet, legal action will be taken following an investigation if a written complaint is submitted.
